booting.text: Come in — give me a second, the desk is still opening.

no_account.text: Come in. Nothing in the vault needs my decision until you have an account — Iris will open one.

lore.text: Come in. Today this desk is for decoration — the branch has no manager service open. Bob releases at the vault window once the clock runs down, and nobody skips the cooling.

vault_only.text: Come in. The priority desk isn't open for your account — either this branch runs vault-only, or Iris still has to re-check your file. I can still shred a wire.

why_vault_only.text: A priority release needs META_APPROVE permissions on your account's transfer function — you sign, I submit. Vault-only accounts deliberately carry none, so the only way out of the vault is the path the contract time-checks. If your file is simply behind the current role set, Iris's re-check adds the split.

idle.text: Come in. {pending} wire(s) in the vault, {cooling} still cooling. {priority_copy} Or I can shred one.

priority_list.text: Which one? Your hand scan authorises it; my desk submits it before the clock. {priority_copy}

not_cooling.text: Those have finished cooling — Bob releases them at the vault window, no hand scan needed. I don't stamp after the clock.

cancel_list.text: Which one goes in the shredder?

priority_ok.text: Released. Wire #{txId} left the vault with {release_in} still on the clock — your hand scan, my stamp. Balance on your account now {balance} {symbol}.

why_priority.text: A priority release is a meta-transaction. You signed an approval for that exact record with your own key — the hand scan guards that key — and my BRANCH_MANAGER role submitted it. The contract lets this path skip releaseTime by design, which is why the branch never lets the silent teller signer sign it: its policy only covers counter slips. Fine print: once an account carries these permissions, any cooling wire on it can leave this way — always under your scan, never without.

cancelled.text: Shredded. Wire #{txId} is recalled; nothing left the vault.

limits.text: Over the counter: up to {limit} {symbol}, done in one step. Above that: the vault, {timelock} of cooling, then Bob releases it — or you bring a hand scan here and I release it early. The counter sets the amount limit; the vault keeps its own clock.

why_limits.text: Your session signer could technically sign an over-the-counter slip for any amount to a whitelisted target — the policy cannot read the amount inside the call data. So routing large amounts to the vault is a Teller Desk rule, stated as a partial invariant in our review. What is enforced on chain: who may request, approve and cancel, that a timed approval waits for releaseTime, and that a priority release needs two different roles — one to sign, one to submit.

why_manager.text: I hold a runtime role — BRANCH_MANAGER. I cannot start a payment. I cannot open the vault after the clock — that is Bob's window, and the chain would refuse me anyway; my timed stamp was removed. I can shred a wire, or submit a priority release before the clock when you bring a hand scan.
